title: Resource fairness — 45° rotational self-overlay proves the 8-fold invariant
attestation: Independent round-6 re-verification of the p1-09 fairness invariant, done with my own eyes this session. Method: I took the live frozen field-map.png (sha 88d36be, the whole 3600² arena in one frame), thresholded it to a binary mask of every bright body (asteroids + planet discs), then ROTATED that mask by exactly 45° (=2π/8, the player count N=8) about the arena collapse centre — which the freeze geometry projects to screen (1032,1800): CENTER world (1200,1200), ship at rest (1968,1200), 3600px viewport. I composited the original mask into the RED channel and the 45°-rotated mask into the GREEN channel. WHAT IS ON SCREEN: the overlay is almost entirely YELLOW — i.e. red and green coincide. All eight home planets around the ring land yellow (only a thin red/green fringe on their differently-coloured beacon rings, which is expected — the beacon hue is the ONE thing that is not rotation-invariant). Every asteroid cluster is solid yellow: each rock has a partner exactly 45° around, and there is NO orphan red-only or green-only asteroid anywhere. That is the fairness invariant SEEN directly: the entire field maps onto itself under a 2π/N turn, so all eight home neighbourhoods are identical rotated copies and the central commons is N-fold symmetric — no planet is favoured. This is a derived analysis image (my own threshold+rotate of the real captured frame), not a raw game screenshot, and I state that plainly; it corroborates fair-home-resources and central-commons.
